title: Side-to-side lace shawl
subtitle: A fingering-weight shawl worked sideways, with a lace panel along the long straight edge.
excerpt: A fingering-weight shawl worked from tip to tip across the wingspan, with a travelling vine lace panel along the straight top edge. Width is cast on and decreased to shape the lower curve; the lace panel is grafted on at the end. Wingspan approximately 145 cm, centre-back depth approximately 55 cm. About 280 g of fingering yarn.
sourceNotes: Side-to-side (asymmetric) shawl construction is a contemporary approach documented in various independent design publications from 2010 onwards. The travelling vine lace border is a traditional lace motif documented in Barbara Walker, A Treasury of Knitting Patterns (1968). The combination of side-to-side shaping with a knitted-on vine lace edge is an original synthesis.

glossaryTerms.definition: A shawl knitted across the wingspan from one tip to the other, rather than from the neck down or from a centre spine. The depth is shaped by adding or removing stitches at the lower edge as the knitting progresses across the width.
A traditional lace pattern in which yarn-overs and decreases are staggered across successive rows to create a sinuous diagonal vine effect. A 10-stitch, 8-row repeat is typical.

content.text: , from the left tip across to the right tip. The main body is plain garter. A 10-stitch deep
panel runs along the straight top edge throughout. Wingspan approximately 145 cm.

The shaping comes from increases then decreases at the lower edge. Cast on 10 stitches for the first tip. Work a double increase every RS row to maximum depth, then work flat to the midpoint. Then work a double decrease every RS row back to 10 stitches for the second tip. Budget about 280 g (about 1,120 m / 1,220 yards) of fingering yarn.

content.text: 26 stitches and 44 rows to 10 cm over vine lace on 3.5 mm needles, blocked. At gauge the maximum depth of approximately 55 cm is reached after approximately 143 increase rows (55 × 2.6 = 143). Two stitches are added per RS row (one each side of the garter body). The maximum stitch count is approximately 143 × 2 + 10 = 296 stitches at midpoint.
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 10 stitches. The first 10 stitches are the vine lace panel: place markers before stitch 1 and after stitch 10. Knit 2 WS rows.

RS row: work vine lace across 10 lace panel sts, SM, yo, k to last st, yo, k1. (2 stitches added.) WS row: k1, p to lace panel marker, SM, work WS lace row. Continue the RS increase row every RS row until the total stitch count reaches approximately 296 (approximately 143 increase rows). The lace panel always occupies the first 10 stitches; the garter body grows from behind the right marker.

Vine lace panel (10 sts, 8-row repeat): RS Row 1: k1, yo, k3, k2tog, k2, yo, k1. RS Row 3: k2, yo, k2, k2tog, k1, yo, k2. RS Row 5: k2, ssk, k2, yo, k2, yo, k1, k1. RS Row 7: k1, ssk, k3, yo, k3, k1. WS rows 2, 4, 6, 8: p all sts within the lace panel.
After reaching maximum depth, work 20 rows without increase or decrease at the lower edge, continuing the vine lace panel throughout.

RS row: work vine lace across 10 lace panel sts, SM, k2tog, k to last 3 sts, ssk, k1. (2 stitches removed.) Continue until 10 stitches remain. Knit 2 WS rows over the remaining 10 lace-panel stitches.
Work Jeny's surprisingly stretchy bind-off across the remaining 10 stitches.

Lace panel stitch count drifting: a yarn-over from the lace pattern was not compensated by its paired decrease. The vine lace panel must always total 10 stitches at the end of every 8-row repeat. Count the lace panel stitches between the markers every 8 rows.

Lower edge not a clean curve: the yo increase or ssk decrease was worked one stitch inside the edge rather than at the outermost position. The increase yo must be worked immediately after the lace panel marker; the decrease ssk sits immediately before the last stitch.

Soak 20 minutes in cool water. Pin the top straight edge fully flat to 145 cm first. Pin the curved lower edge, easing out the extra length over the second half of the shawl. The vine lace panel opens significantly with blocking.
Hand wash in cool water and lay flat to dry. Re-block after washing to restore the lace open.
Replace the plain garter body with an eyelet grid: k1, yo, k2tog across every 4th RS row. This gives allover lace at about the same construction difficulty as the plain version.
